subject: Packaging choices for Pilot — upgrade cadence & bundled features
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@pulsecare.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Khatri <amira.k@pulsecare.health>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options for our 6-week pilot

Ben —

Thanks for the product demo last week. Amira and I reviewed the notes and we have two packaging concerns before we sign the pilot SOW: 1) our legal wants clarity about the ability to increase committed capacity mid-pilot without re-contracting, and 2) our clinical team will likely want access to additional features (reranking + structured output) in week 3 if the initial evaluation looks good.

Can you summarize the upgrade cadence and whether feature bundles can be toggled and billed pro-rata for just the remaining pilot weeks? I've attached a short requirements sheet.

Also: any recommended default bundle for a telemetry-forward pilot (high embedding volume + live inference)?

Appreciate a short options list — we need to get internal buy-in by Wednesday.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of AI Integrations
PulseCare Health

Attachment: PulseCare_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@pulsecare.health>
Cc: Amira Khatri <amira.k@pulsecare.health>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for our 6-week pilot

Tom —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the sheet — helpful. Short summary up front, then details:

TL;DR options (pick A or B):
- Option A — Flexible Pilot (recommended): start on our Compact Pilot bundle; you can increase committed capacity mid-pilot (one business-day notice) and we prorate additional committed units for the remainder of the term. Bundled features (reranking / structured output) can be enabled as an add-on; you pay for add-on pro-rata from the enablement date. No re-contract required.
- Option B — Committed Pilot (for predictability): sign a short addendum to lock the higher capacity from day 1; cleaner budget but requires a one-email amendment.

Notes and caveats:
- Auto-scaling vs committed: autoscaling can cover short spikes without changes; committed gives lower effective unit cost.
- Billing/proration: proration is calculated daily; we bill the remainder of the pilot at the prorated rate on your next invoice.
- Feature gating: we can gate reranking and structured output behind a feature flag and enable it without a contract change. Usage while gated will be billed at the add-on rate; we can set caps for the pilot to keep costs predictable.
- SLA/credits: pilot deployments use our standard Pilot SLA (no financial credits) unless you move to Dedicated.

Suggested default for telemetry-forward pilot: Compact Pilot + Embedding Booster add-on + Structured Output gated (week 3 enable). That combination keeps initial cost low while giving the telemetry team full signal volume.

I'll loop in Lauren from Billing to confirm proration mechanics and Grace from Solutions to help with the gating flow. If you want, we can produce a single-page amendment you can sign digitally that documents the mid-pilot capacity increase flow.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred option (A or B) by EOD Wed.
2) We prepare a 1-page amendment (if B) or a simple change-order template (if A) and a cost estimate for the week-3 feature enable.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119

Attachment: Redwood_pilot-pricing-options.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@pulsecare.health>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Khatri <amira.k@pulsecare.health>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for our 6-week pilot

Team —

Quick billing clarification to support Ben's note:

- If you choose Option A (Flexible Pilot) and ask for a capacity bump mid-pilot, we'll calculate the delta between committed units (pre-bump) and the new committed units, prorate for the remaining pilot days, and invoice the delta on your next monthly invoice.
- If you only enable add-on features without changing committed units (e.g., turn on reranking week 3), we bill the add-on usage at the daily rate and cap at the threshold we agree.
- Payment terms for pilots remain net 30. For the one-page amendment (Option B), we can pre-authorize a charge schedule if you prefer faster activation.

I'll prepare a short example invoice line showing the proration math (delta * remaining days / total pilot days). Ben — want me to attach a sample calculation to the HubSpot deal?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

--
On a related note, Grace — can the gating flow include a UI toggle and an API flag so PulseCare can enable structured output programmatically?

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@pulsecare.health>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for our 6-week pilot

Hi Tom / Amira —

Yes — we can provide both a console UI toggle and an API endpoint to flip the structured-output and reranking features. Implementation plan:
1) We create a pilot feature flag under your account (no code change).
2) We set a soft cap for the first week after enablement and monitor token/embedding consumption.
3) We run an enablement call (15 min) the morning of the planned week-3 switch and stay on the call for the first hour of traffic.

Operational notes:
- If you expect >5x embedding volume week-over-week, tell us now — we'll pre-provision burst capacity to avoid throttling.
- Logging and telemetry: we will stream token-level usage and error traces to your shared S3 bucket for the pilot window.

Tom — if that all looks good, I propose we schedule the enablement call for Aug 20 at 09:00 PT (assuming week 1 starts Aug 6). I'll draft the short runbook for the call.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
